newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Oct 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Oct 1.

text.p: THE DOMINION

Prime Minister Jim Bolger was unrepentant of comments made on Australian television yesterday spurring fears for investors of economic instability if National lost the election. Opposition opponents called the comments "economic sabotage", but Bolger supporters saw the ensuing row as positive as they wanted to steer debate away from social issues. Page 1.
A $40 million deal settling Maori claims arising from land confiscations in Opotiki in 1865 is to be signed in Parliament this morning. Cabinet had approved the deal yesterday. Page 1.

New Zealand First leader Winston Peters is refusing to rule out a post-election deal with National, despite increasing pressure from Labour and the Alliance for him to do so. A One Network News Colmar Brunton poll showed 69 percent of 1,000 people polled wanted to know about possible coalitions before the election. Page 2.

Prime Minster Jim Bolger held out on the prospect of discussions on health with other parties after the election, saying New Zealanders wanted consensus among politicians on the "number one" election issue. National has been softening its approach on health and acknowledged in its television campaign launched last week that they had made mistakes. Page 2.
Alliance leader Jim Anderton vowed to reinstate lump-sum accident compensation up to $128,000 and abolish the ACC earners levy, at a rally in Christchurch yesterday. Page 2.
Labour leader Helen Clark's preferred prime minister rating nearly doubled to 13 percent in a new TV3-CM research poll moving her ahead of Alliance leader Jim Anderton on 11 percent. Page 2.

As many as 1,400 Labour Department staff were likely to start industrial action tomorrow that could result in their suspension, a Public Service Association spokesman said. The department had proposed longer hours and cuts to pay and conditions, which was the worst example of abuse of the Employment COntracts Act, the spokesman said.
Progressive Enterprises' profit slumped 81.4 percent to $3.5 million for the year to July 28, it announced yesterday. The supermarket giant will not pay out a dividend to shareholders. Page 15.

National Bank of New Zealand disclosed a 30 percent drop in first-half net profit to $41 million for the six months to June 30. The lower profit, down from $59 million for the same period last year, was foreshadowed in a staff memo from the chief executive last month. Page 15.

Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp's New Zealand branch expects to maintain performance at present levels after a 306 percent rise in operating profit to $7.04 million for the six months to June. As well as building corporate business, Chief Executive John Blanthorne said the bank intended increasing the amount of mortgage lending.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD

The Jewish community is keeping a cautious eye on New Zealand First's latest campaign move which links hospital waiting lists and mass wartime exterminations. Winston Peters launched a billboard in downtown Auckland yesterday headed "Shipley's List", showing a vast line of people shuffling towards a hospital doorway. A Jewish leader said there were obvious links with the award-winning film on the Nazi Holocaust, "Schindler's List". Page 1.
Prime Minister Jim Bolger quickly faced charges of economic sabotage and scaremongering after telling Australian investors to wait until after polling day before investing in New Zealand. Page 1.
Prime Minister Jim Bolger sought to neutralise his administration's most vunerable policy yesterday, with a call for parties to reach a consensus on health after the election.

The Government and Bay of Plenty Maori are on the verge of completing negotiations to settle an Opotiki land claim. The government offered a $40 million package, which will be approved in cabinet today. Maori met last night to decide whther to sign an agreement today.

The ACT party crossed the 5 percent barrier in a second consecutive public opinion poll, but the figures clearly showed a grouping of Labour, New Zealand First and the Alliance would easily outnumber National and ACT.

New Zealand First said public hospital patients would not wait more than three months for most types of surgery under its policy. The Minister of Health and health officials labelled the move unrealistic.

Georgie Pie restaurants took a $8.5 million bite out of supermarket operator Progressive Enterprises' profit in the year to July 28, which plunged 81 percent to $3.55 million. But managing director Graeme Kelly said the sale of 17 of the 32 Georgie Pie outlets since balance date ensured the same magnitude of loss would not happen this year.
Brierley Investments' share price slipped three cents to $1.38 as indications from Britain suggested that the float price for its Thistle Hotels chain would be lower than expected.
In a surprise move, WEL Energy Group chairman Brian Corban said yesterday he was stepping down from the Hamilton-based electricity supplier's board.
Chaotic trading on financial markets resulting from an flight of overseas capital after the election was likely to be short-lived, dealers and analysts said.
A nationalisation of forest ownership, which is expected to follow the sale of Forestry Corp, could create buying opportunities for Evergreen Forests, its chief executive said.
